input.quote: The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor.
input.rationale: Article IV (p0049) lets the Licensor unilaterally extend the 36-month Initial Period by a further seven years, with no Licensee opt-out or notice window. A one-sided multi-year renewal is walk-away territory under RENEWAL and fails the fallback (no non-renewal notice window at all, renewal term far longer than 60 days' exit / 12 months). It also contradicts the retained mutual-extension mechanics in Article IV.II and IV.III. The shortest cure is to delete the Licensor's unilateral option so renewal (and any renewal pricing) requires mutual written agreement, which meets the preferred position; there is no renewal price-uplift mechanic elsewhere (fee tiers at p0057-p0063 are fixed), so no uplift cap is needed.

proposal.summary: Renewal only by mutual written agreement; delete Licensor's unilateral 7-year renewal option.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the Licensor's unilateral option to extend for a further seven years so that any renewal (including its pricing) requires mutual written agreement, consistent with the balance of Article IV. Our playbook treats one-sided multi-year renewals as unacceptable.

ops.oldText: The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor.
ops.newText: The Agreement may be renewed only by mutual written agreement of the parties.

mappings.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
